steps.title: Styles instead of loose formatting
steps.body: Don't make headings bigger and bolder by hand — use Styles (the 'Home' tab): Heading 1, Heading 2, Normal. That way your document looks consistent everywhere, and you can change all headings with one click later.

steps.title: Lists, tables and margins
steps.body: Use bullet points for lists and Insert > Table for overviews (like a quote). Under Layout you set margins and orientation. Add page numbers via Insert > Page Number for longer documents.

steps.title: Templates, checking and PDF
steps.body: Don't start from a blank page every time: under 'New' choose a template for a letter, résumé or invoice. Let the spell checker (F7) run. Sending the document to someone else? Save it as a PDF (File > Save as) so the layout stays intact.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Make a short quote or letter with a Heading 1, a table with three rows and page numbers, and also save it as a PDF.

steps.title: Using formulas
steps.body: A formula always starts with =. Examples: =SUM(B2:B10) adds up, =AVERAGE(B2:B10) gives the average, and =B2*C2 multiplies two cells. Refer to cells instead of typing numbers: if a number changes, Excel recalculates by itself.

steps.title: Sorting, filtering and frozen headers
steps.body: Select your table and choose Data > Filter to sort and filter (for example all expenses above €50). With View > Freeze Panes your top row stays visible while scrolling.

steps.title: Making a chart
steps.body: Select your data and choose Insert > Chart. A bar chart works well for comparing (spending per month), a pie chart for splitting up (where does my money go). Give the chart a clear title.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Make a household budget for three months, calculate totals and the average with formulas, and add a chart.

steps.title: One message per slide
steps.body: Put one point on each slide, with short text and preferably an image rather than a wall of text. A good rule: no more than six lines per slide. Don't read your slides out word for word — add something to them.

steps.title: Design and layout
steps.body: Choose a theme under Design and stick to it: the same colors and fonts on all slides. Use the built-in layouts (Home > Layout) instead of dragging text boxes around yourself. Add a chart or photo where it helps.

steps.title: Presenting with confidence
steps.body: Use the notes under your slide for your talking points, and practice once out loud. With Present (F5) you see the slides full screen; during a video meeting you can share your screen. Save a copy as a PDF to share afterwards.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Make a five-slide presentation for a work meeting or neighborhood meeting, with a theme, one chart and notes on every slide.
